extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing writers looking for classes or programs (Boston-area and online)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for choosing and understanding GrubStreet creative-writing offerings (multi-week workshops, short classes, intensives, teen programs, and online formats), including structure, feedback expectations, and prerequisites. Useful for prospective students deciding which class type fits their goals and schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-Week Workshops — meeting cadence and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-week workshops are offered in every genre, and typically meet once a week for three hours, for anywhere from four to ten weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They meet either over Zoom or in-person at our Center for Creative Writing in Boston. Use this format for ongoing continuity and to develop work over multiple sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-Week Workshops — range of feedback and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops range from generative classes with light feedback, to advanced classes with a focus on revision and in-depth written feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a generative class if you want idea-generation and light critique; choose an advanced/revision-focused workshop if you want in-depth written feedback and revision guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Classes — format and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Short classes meet one time, for three or six hours, usually on weekend days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They take place on Zoom and in-person at the Center. Short classes are appropriate for focused skill workshops or single-topic deep dives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Classes — breadth of topics and genres
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer several short classes every week, and you’ll find short classes in every genre, on every topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short classes to explore specific techniques, genres, or topics without committing to a multi-week course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Experience — delivery modes
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer both live Zoom classes and asynchronous classes that you can complete on your own time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All are instructor-led and community-based. Online options aim to bring the GrubStreet classroom experience to remote students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teen Program (YAWP) — program types and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Young Adult Writers Program (YAWP) offers three types of programs: free Saturday writing sessions, Teen Writing Classes (during winter, spring, and summer vacations), and a three-week summer Teen Writing Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for high school students from the greater Boston area to craft stories, share ideas, and receive peer support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensives — immersive advanced study
rubrics_metrics.description: Intensives provide greater continuity and an immersive, intensive exploration of craft as you develop and revise a book-length project or collection of stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced programs in the novel, memoir, and the short story are recommended for writers working on longer manuscripts who want concentrated revision and mentorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite / experience expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do I need prior writing experience to join? Not at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GrubStreet offers beginner-friendly classes designed to help you take your very first steps into writing; select level-appropriate offerings if you are a novice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Will I get feedback on my writing? Yes! Most classes include peer and instructor feedback sessions, which are central to the learning experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect group critique and instructor commentary as core components; intensity and format of feedback vary by class type (light vs. in-depth written feedback).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking multiple classes for continued growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I take multiple classes? Absolutely. Many students take multiple classes across genres or skill levels to continue growing their craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix genres and levels to broaden skills or deepen focus; scheduling and prerequisites should be checked per course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic / modality note
rubrics_metrics.description: Classes meet either over Zoom or in-person at our Center for Creative Writing in Boston.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not live in Boston, the online experience (live or asynchronous) is intended to provide comparable instruction and community.
